answers: lens-correctness-design finding 1: wrong — The design already addresses this. Gap 11 in the Context/gaps section documents the problem explicitly: after `skip_until_stage` is cleared when the from-stage target unit is found (in both the cycle:* arm and the stage:* arm of the dispatch-unit loop in `main()` in runner.sh), `resume_mode` is also immediately set to `false`. The fix is `[[ -n "$skip_until_stage" ]] && { skip_until_stage=""; resume_mode=false; }` in both arms. This prevents the resume skip guard (`$resume_mode && [[ -z "$skip_until_stage" ]]`) from activating for all subsequent stages after `<s>` — leaf or cycle. DSFSTG-3[code] pins the observable behavior with a 3-unit fixture [intake (leaf), cyc (cycle), verify (leaf)]: when all three are marked complete in an interrupted run and the runner is invoked with `--resume --from-stage cyc`, stage.start is emitted for verify even though it was marked complete; the test fails on old code (verify skipped because `resume_mode` stays `true`) and passes after the fix (`resume_mode=false` releases the guard). The Decision paragraph and Finding 30/31 also document this explicitly. The finding describes a real gap; the design's answer is the Gap 11 fix and DSFSTG-3[code].
